chill.title: Art Nouveau Bathing at Centralbadet
chill.description: A 1904 Jugendstil bathhouse hidden behind a courtyard garden on Drottninggatan — stained glass, a colonnaded pool and saunas, with phones banned throughout.
chill.bonus: Do the full circuit — sauna, cold, pool, repeat — three times.

chill.title: Sculpture Terraces at Millesgården
chill.description: Carl Milles built his home into a Lidingö cliff and filled the terraces with bronze figures that appear to be launching off the edge over the water.
chill.bonus: Find the sculpture that looks best against the sky and sit with it.

chill.title: An Afternoon in the Woodland Cemetery
chill.description: Skogskyrkogården is a UNESCO site and one of the great works of 20th-century architecture — pine forest, a grass hill and Asplund's chapels arranged for quiet.
chill.bonus: Walk up the Hill of Remembrance and sit under the elms.

chill.title: Second-Hand Hunting Around Söderhallarna
chill.description: Work the vintage and second-hand shops clustered around Medborgarplatsen and Söderhallarna, where Stockholm's famously good charity shops actually get their stock.
chill.bonus: Buy one thing you would never have chosen new.

chill.title: A Slow Hour on Mariatorget
chill.description: A leafy Södermalm square with a fountain, benches and cafes on every side — the neighbourhood's living room, best used with a coffee and no plan.
chill.bonus: Stay long enough to watch the square turn over completely.

chill.title: Sunset from Herman's Terrace
chill.description: A vegetarian buffet on a cliff-edge terrace on Fjällgatan, with the whole harbour, Djurgården and the ferries laid out below your plate.
chill.bonus: Get there an hour before sunset to claim a rail seat.

culture.title: A Thousand Years of Sweden at Nordiska Museet
culture.description: A vast Renaissance-revival hall on Djurgården holding Swedish domestic life since 1520, with a giant painted Gustav Vasa presiding over the main floor.
culture.bonus: Find the Sámi collection on the upper floor — most visitors miss it.

culture.title: Ride the Blue Line Art Gallery
culture.description: Stockholm's metro is the longest art gallery on earth — blasted rock caverns painted at Kungsträdgården, Solna Centrum and T-Centralen, all for the price of a ticket.
culture.bonus: Get off at four stations you had no reason to visit.

culture.title: Drottningholm Palace and Its Court Theatre
culture.description: Take the steamboat across Mälaren to a UNESCO royal residence whose 1766 theatre still uses its original hand-cranked wooden stage machinery.
culture.bonus: Take the theatre tour, not just the palace one.

culture.title: A Night at the Royal Swedish Opera
culture.description: Gold, red velvet and a painted ceiling on Gustav Adolfs torg, where Sweden's national opera and ballet perform in a house built in 1898 for exactly this.
culture.bonus: Buy the cheapest seat in the house and dress for the most expensive one.

culture.title: Old Sweden Outdoors at Skansen
culture.description: The world's first open-air museum — 150 buildings moved here from across the country and staffed in period, plus bears, wolves and lynx in the Nordic zoo.
culture.bonus: Find the oldest building on the site and go inside it.

culture.title: The Nationalmuseum After Dark
culture.description: Sweden's national gallery reopened after a five-year restoration with its colours put back — Rembrandt, Swedish 19th-century painting and a famously good design collection.
culture.bonus: Find Carl Larsson's enormous staircase mural and work out what is happening in it.

culture.title: The Royal Armoury Beneath the Palace
culture.description: In the cellar vaults of the Royal Palace: coronation carriages, tournament armour and the actual blood-stained clothes kings died in, which is a great deal stranger than it sounds.
culture.bonus: Time it with the changing of the guard in the outer courtyard.

culture.title: Modern Art on Skeppsholmen
culture.description: Moderna Museet holds Picasso, Dalí and Rauschenberg on a small navy island, with Niki de Saint Phalle's sculptures outside and a restaurant view across the water.
culture.bonus: Have lunch in the museum restaurant for the view alone.

social.title: Belgian Beer and Whisky at Akkurat
social.description: A Hornsgatan institution with hundreds of bottles, a wall of single malts and a cellar of lambics — the bar Swedish beer nerds send everyone to first.
social.bonus: Ask for a gueuze and drink it without flinching.

social.title: See a Band at Debaser Strand
social.description: Hornstull's mid-size live room, named after a Pixies song, where Swedish bands break and touring acts play the night before the big venues.
social.bonus: Buy a ticket for a band you have never heard of.

social.title: Sunset Cocktails at Himlen Skybar
social.description: The twenty-sixth floor of Skrapan tower in Södermalm, with a wraparound bar and the only 360-degree view over Stockholm you can drink in.
social.bonus: Do a full lap of the windows before you order.

social.title: Live Jazz at Fasching
social.description: Stockholm's main jazz room since 1977, a narrow hall off Kungsgatan that runs international bookings early and turns into a club night afterwards.
social.bonus: Stay for the club night after the band finishes.

social.title: Hockey Night at Avicii Arena
social.description: The world's largest spherical building, packed for a Djurgården or AIK game, with a standing end that sings for a full sixty minutes.
social.bonus: Sit in the standing end, not the neutral seats.

social.title: Beers in the Old Hall at Kvarnen
social.description: A 1908 beer hall on Södermalm with vaulted ceilings and long shared tables, the historic home of Hammarby supporters and loud in the best possible way.
social.bonus: Go on a Hammarby matchday and see what happens.

social.title: Cocktails and Late Tacos at Tjoget
social.description: A Hornstull complex holding a serious cocktail bar, a wine room, a taqueria and a barber under one roof — the sort of place an evening accidentally lasts in.
social.bonus: Move between three of the rooms in one night.

social.title: A Full Night at Trädgården
social.description: An enormous open-air club built under the concrete arches of Skanstullsbron each summer — several stages, table tennis, food trucks and the whole city's twenty-somethings.
social.bonus: Stay until the sky starts getting light again. In June it barely stops.

8ball.title: Buy the Next Person's Fika
8ball.description: Fika is not a coffee break, it is the social contract — so pay for whoever is behind you in the queue and see whether they will sit down with you.

8ball.title: Board the First Ferry That Docks
8ball.description: Stockholm is fourteen islands and the boats are public transport — get on whichever one arrives first and disembark wherever it decides to put you.
8ball.bonus: Do not check the destination board before boarding.

foodie.title: Cardamom Buns at Fabrique
foodie.description: A stone-oven bakery in a tiled Södermalm basement where the cardamom buns come out in trays all morning and the smell reaches the street.
foodie.bonus: Eat it warm, standing up, within sight of the oven.

foodie.title: Fika at Vete-Katten
foodie.description: A 1928 konditori that runs back through a warren of parlour rooms to a hidden courtyard, serving the princess cake and cinnamon buns Stockholm measures all others against.
foodie.bonus: Find the back courtyard rather than sitting at the front.

foodie.title: The Tasting Menu at Frantzén
foodie.description: Three Michelin stars over three floors of a restored townhouse, beginning in the kitchen itself — Sweden's most decorated restaurant and a genuine event of a night.
foodie.bonus: Take the kitchen counter seats if they are offered.

foodie.title: Everything Cooked Over Fire at Ekstedt
foodie.description: A Michelin kitchen with no electricity in it — every course comes off a wood fire, a birch-fired oven, a flaming birch pit or a smoking chimney, in front of you.
foodie.bonus: Ask which course was the hardest to cook without a thermostat.

foodie.title: Pizza and Sour Beer at Omnipollos hatt
foodie.description: Stockholm's cult brewery pairs its fruited sours and hazy IPAs with thin, blistered pizza in a small tiled room on Hornsgatan.
foodie.bonus: Order the strangest-sounding beer on the board and match a pizza to it.

foodie.title: Sausage and Mash from Günter's Korvar
foodie.description: A cult sausage kiosk on Karlbergsvägen with a permanent queue and a rotating board of wildly specific German and Swedish sausages served in a bun or with mash.
foodie.bonus: Order whatever is written on the specials board, no questions.

foodie.title: Toast Skagen at Sturehof
foodie.description: A grand old Stureplan brasserie with a marble seafood bar, where the prawn-and-dill toast on rye is the single most Stockholm thing you can order.
foodie.bonus: Sit at the bar rather than a table and watch them shuck.

foodie.title: Get a Table at Lilla Ego
foodie.description: The hardest small booking in Stockholm — a Vasastan neighbourhood restaurant doing big, generous, unfussy Swedish cooking that locals plan their month around.
foodie.bonus: Call the moment the booking window opens and take whatever time they give you.

adventure.title: Sunset from the Cliffs of Skinnarviksberget
adventure.description: Scramble up the highest natural point in central Stockholm, a bare granite outcrop on Södermalm where the whole city drinks cans and watches the light go down over Mälaren.
adventure.bonus: Get to the very top rock rather than the easy ledge.

adventure.title: Climb the Wooden Streets of Åsöberget
adventure.description: A hillside of 18th-century wooden cottages and steep alleys on Södermalm that survived every demolition plan, with views down over the harbour from the top of every stair.
adventure.bonus: Find Stigbergsgatan and follow the smallest alley off it.

adventure.title: Sail Out to Sandhamn in the Outer Archipelago
adventure.description: Take the Waxholmsbolaget boat three hours east through thousands of islands to a sailing village of red huts, white sand and open Baltic on every side.
adventure.bonus: Swim off the rocks on the seaward side, not the harbour.

adventure.title: Ferry to Vaxholm and Its Island Fortress
adventure.description: An hour up the inner archipelago to a pastel wooden town, with a granite fortress on its own island guarding the channel and a short boat hop to reach it.
adventure.bonus: Take the little cable ferry across to the fortress rather than looking at it.

adventure.title: Rooftop Walk Above Riddarholmen
adventure.description: Clip into a safety line and walk the ridge of a 17th-century government roof forty-three metres above the old town, with nothing between you and Lake Mälaren.
adventure.bonus: Let go of the rail with both hands, once.

adventure.title: Forest, Lake and Sauna at Hellasgården
adventure.description: Twenty minutes by bus into Nacka's nature reserve for pine forest trails, a swimming lake and a wood-fired sauna the locals use in every season including February.
adventure.bonus: Sauna, then get into the lake. In winter, through the hole in the ice.

adventure.title: Boat to Fjäderholmarna, the Nearest Island
adventure.description: Twenty-five minutes from Slussen and you are on a proper archipelago island with craft workshops, a smokehouse and rocks to swim from.
adventure.bonus: Eat smoked fish straight from the smokehouse on the rocks.

adventure.title: Walk Djurgården's Wild Far End
adventure.description: Keep walking past the museums to Blockhusudden, where the royal park turns into oak forest and open water and the crowds disappear entirely.
adventure.bonus: Walk until you cannot hear a single car.
